implemented_component: Synthetic laboratory, transport and human event generators; scenario JSON event stream
inputs: Ordered scenario steps with synthetic result, transport, patient and supervisor events
evidence_of_existence: 7 scenario files, 51 ordered steps in total
limitations: Sources are fabricated fixtures, not live feed handlers. No telecom data source exists.

implemented_component: Event ingestion and append-only event store
outputs: Persisted event row with seq, at, kind, actor, source_layer
evidence_of_existence: events table populated for every run; exported in the audit bundle
limitations: Collector is in-process; no queue, no backpressure handling, no multi-tenant isolation.

implemented_component: Normalisation, schema validation, scope and revision tagging of incoming events
outputs: Typed MachineContext with current revision, attempts, acknowledgments, scope
evidence_of_existence: Every guard reads MachineContext; malformed agent output is rejected by Pydantic
limitations: Preprocessing is rule-based; no anomaly detection on the event stream.

implemented_component: Five role-scoped agents producing validated structured assessments
evidence_of_existence: Each agent has distinct allowed_fields and a distinct assessment contract
limitations: Agents are deterministic rule engines in this build. No LLM provider is wired in; the 'model' analogy is structural, not statistical.

framework_definition_source: ITU-T Y.3172 §8.1, p15 - 'applies policies to the output of the model node'
implemented_component: Deterministic gate: invariants, scope decision, approval withholding
evidence_of_existence: No agent can move state directly; every consequential action passes enforce()
limitations: The gate is code, not a policy language; changing it requires a code change and review.

implemented_component: Simulated transport adapter with idempotency, channel authorisation and reconciliation
outputs: Attempt record, provider events, delivery receipts, reconciliation outcomes
evidence_of_existence: REAL_NETWORK_ACCESS = False asserted in /api/health; no sockets are opened
limitations: Simulation only; no real SMS/portal gateway, no carrier semantics, no delivery-report lag modelling beyond the script.

implemented_component: Synthetic patient endpoint, supervisor queue, communication record
outputs: Mock delivery target state, escalation ticket, documentation record
evidence_of_existence: Escalation tickets and documentation records persisted per case
limitations: No human is actually notified. The 'patient' is a synthetic reference string.

implemented_component: Orchestration engine: dispatch, context scoping, proposal resolution, audit
outputs: Per-step record: assessments, gate decision, transitions, unresolved questions
evidence_of_existence: Documented in docs/architecture.md and exposed at /api/meta/state-machine
limitations: Single-process orchestrator; no distributed placement, no model selection, no performance-based reselection as Y.3172 envisages.

framework_concept: Separation of ML pipeline from underlay (conceptual)
implemented_component: No separate underlay: the transport simulator is in-process
limitations: NOT IMPLEMENTED. ResultRelay does not implement an ML overlay/underlay split and claims no Y.3172 conformance.

framework_concept: P (policy) constrained by an external legal layer
framework_definition_source: ITU-T Y.3172 (06/2019) §8.1, p15 - the policy node applies policies to model output
implemented_component: The policy node is implemented as deterministic rules, and the rules it may apply are bounded before ranking by jurisdiction and claim class
inputs: Retrieved chunks with jurisdiction and claim_classification, plus the case jurisdiction
outputs: Only AE-DU/AE-FED material may become binding for a Dubai case; other material is comparator-only and cannot reach the action
evidence_of_existence: 56 chunks across 13 sources of which the binding classes are confined to two jurisdictions; retriever widens a case jurisdiction upwards to the federal layer only
limitations: Y.3172 says nothing about law. The mapping is architectural (where the constraint sits), not a compliance claim: a policy node that is legally bounded is still not a legal opinion.

implemented_component: The proposed adviser, if enabled, runs behind the unchanged deterministic gate and can only propose; every proposal is classified PRODUCT_DESIGN_CONTROL and re-checked against the gate
outputs: A proposal that the gate may reject, downgrade or mark as needing evidence
evidence_of_existence: Deterministic mode is the default; the sandbox analogy is used only to describe containment, and is labelled as an analogy
demonstrating_test: Not implemented - the adviser is disabled, so containment is designed and untested
limitations: Art. 13 of Federal Law 2/2019 governs where such a model may run, which Y.3172 does not address. The residency question is recorded in R16 and GR-13's sibling row, and remains open.
